provider: Source Cooperative - uncapped public publishing, beta-gated

free_tier.stated: No published byte cap: 'allowing trusted organizations and individuals to publish data of any kind at any scale'. Case study: Earth Genome publishes 60+ TB. Platform total reported at just over 5 PB.

egress.terms: Free public reads through the data proxy at data.source.coop - live probe returned HTTP 200 with Cloudflare in front (CF-RAY present), so reads are CDN-covered.

tooling: Objects served at data.source.coop/<account>/<product>/...; the proxy is open source (Rust, github.com/source-cooperative/data.source.coop). Bring Your Own Bucket (BYOB) points Source at an S3 bucket you own, read via OIDC federation (sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity) with no long-lived secret either side.
chaining: Per data product, owned by 'an organization or an individual' explicitly. BYOB is the important primitive: it decouples the catalogue/CDN from the bytes, so a free bucket elsewhere becomes a Source product with Cloudflare-fronted reads.
limits_note: Beta: publishing requires acceptance as a beta tester via a Google Form, and BYOB requires Source staff to enable it per account ('contact hello@source.coop'). Public-only by design - 'all data hosted in Source is available to the public'. New products default to Unlisted.
reliability_note: Nonprofit (Radiant Earth 501(c)(3) parent) with in-kind AWS/Azure; beta terms can change. Storage itself lives on commodity cloud, so durability is AWS-grade.
